what: The Business Name Generator gives you 48 name ideas at a time from your own keywords. Choose your industry, from tech and food to fitness, consulting or pet care, and a style: brandable invented words, professional names, fun names or short one-word names.

Every idea shows matching web addresses with the endings you pick, including global ones like .com, .io and .shop and country ones like .co.uk, .ca, .com.au, .de or .in. These are suggestions only; the tool does not check availability.
Tap a name to copy it and tap the star to keep it in your favourites, which are saved on this device. Copy your shortlist with its domains when you are ready to check them.
uses: Find a name for a shop, studio, agency or online store.
Get short brandable names for a product or app.
Explore fresh names that keep a key word.
Find a name that also works as a handle and web address.
Share a shortlist of favourites to vote on.
tutorial: Enter one to three words, such as "coffee, green" or "bright, tutor". Accents are removed for domain ideas.
The industry adds suitable words, such as Kitchen for food or Labs for tech.
Pick Mix, Brandable, Professional, Fun or Short, and the longest name you want.
Tick the endings you would like to see under each name.
Press Generate names. Press again for a new batch.
Tap a name to copy it, star it to save it, and use Copy favourites to copy your list with domains.
features: Industry words that fit your field.
Brandable, professional, fun and short, or a mix.
20 global and country endings to choose from.
Saved on this device and copied in one click.

example.title: Worked example: a name for a coffee cart
example.text: Leila types "coffee, green", chooses Food and drink and the Mix style, and ticks .com and .ca. Among the ideas she sees Green Pantry, Coffeenest and Cheeky Coffee with greencoffeeco.com style addresses under each. She stars four, copies the list and checks the domains and Canada's business name register before choosing.

tips: Say the name out loud and check it is easy to spell after hearing it once.
Search the name in your country's trademark database before you register it.
Check that the matching social media handles are free too.
Shorter names are easier to remember and fit better on signs and logos.
Avoid names that only make sense in one language if you plan to sell abroad.
problems: Your keywords are long and the length limit is short. Choose a longer "Longest name" or a shorter keyword.
Add a keyword about what you sell, and pick your industry instead of "Any business".
This tool cannot see registrations. Try another ending, add a word like "get" or "hq", or pick another favourite.
